orgs.name: A NEW LEAF INC
services: East Valley Men's Center (2345 N Country Club Dr, Mesa): 104-bed emergency shelter for men 18+ experiencing homelessness — stays up to 120 days with a bed and secure storage, a personalized housing stability plan, case management, employment assistance (resumes, references, job interviews), transportation assistance, financial literacy, counseling and behavioral-health referrals, substance-abuse support-group referrals, health/dental referrals, and veteran resources. Prescreen online; shelter placement line for individuals: (877) 211-8661

La Mesita (Mesa): family homeless shelter plus affordable and permanent supportive housing, with weekly case management, employment assistance, financial literacy, counseling, and preschool/after-school programming (City of Mesa / A New Leaf published materials)
Rapid Rehousing (per A New Leaf's own all-services sheet): rental assistance and case management to move households into housing

Also on its own services sheet: Homeward Bound family shelter, Autumn House and Faith House domestic-violence shelters, DV court advocacy, sexual-violence support services and helpline (480) 733-3028, and MesaCAN — Mesa's community-action door for financial empowerment and assistance (635 E Broadway Rd, Mesa)
orgs.serves: men, families, and domestic-violence survivors facing homelessness in Mesa and the East Valley

orgs.name: ANDRE HOUSE OF ARIZONA INC
services: Hospitality center for people experiencing homelessness in downtown Phoenix (213 S 11th Ave, across from the Key Campus), in the Congregation of Holy Cross / Catholic Worker tradition — guests are welcomed with dignity, no program enrollment required
Evening meal service six nights a week (Sat-Thu 5:30-6:30 PM per its published service listing), serving on average about 600 plates a night — more than 170,000 meals a year
Showers (Mon-Thu and Sat afternoons), a free clothing closet, laundry services, blankets and backpacks, lockers, and emergency food-box distribution to neighbors

Its own history page also names: a house welcoming homeless women (since 1987), education and recreation programs for neighborhood children, and basic first-aid/medication help and legal services described in Notre Dame's program account of Andre House
orgs.serves: people experiencing homelessness and poverty in downtown Phoenix

orgs.name: CATHOLIC CHARITIES COMMUNITY SERVICES INC
services: MANA House: transitional housing and supportive services for veterans who have experienced homelessness (Phoenix)
My Sisters' Place & Pathways: domestic-violence shelter and services (Chandler)
Housing for Hope affordable housing communities and resident services
Community Re-Entry services for people returning from incarceration; DIGNITY Diversion program
PATH homeless outreach
Familias Unidas immigration legal services
Counseling on a sliding fee scale; Arizona Families F.I.R.S.T. substance-use family program
Foster care licensing, adoption, in-home family preservation and Westside Head Start early education
Refugee resettlement services; Medical Loan Closet
orgs.serves: Vulnerable people of all faiths in central and northern Arizona — veterans, domestic-violence survivors, families, refugees and immigrants, people reentering from incarceration

orgs.name: CENTRAL ARIZONA SHELTER SERVICES INC
services: Arizona's largest emergency shelter provider (founded 1984): same-day emergency shelter placement for single adults 18+ at the Key Campus shelter, 230 S 12th Ave, Phoenix (subject to availability), with basic-needs support and case-management onboarding toward stable housing
Vista Colina Family Shelter: private-room family shelter — families enter through the Family Housing Hub (call 211 first)
The Haven: Arizona's first dedicated emergency shelter for adults 55+, with age-aware, accessible care
Showers, hygiene, and daily meals for shelter guests (limited walk-in access during posted hours); secure mail services — use CASS as a mailing address while unhoused
Rapid Re-housing: short-term rental assistance, case management, and tenancy support to secure housing quickly or avoid returning to homelessness
Benefits & Identification help: obtaining IDs, Social Security cards, and birth certificates, and enrolling in AHCCCS/Medicaid, SNAP, or other benefits; help replacing critical documents at intake
Veterans: case management and housing assistance tailored to veterans, coordinated with the VA and SSVF programs

Employment & Education support (resumes, job training, workforce partners); healthcare navigation to primary, urgent, and behavioral-health care; behavioral-health and recovery screenings with referrals to counseling and treatment; transportation assistance — bus passes or referrals may be available through case management; domestic-violence safety-planning referrals
orgs.serves: single adults, families with children, older adults 55+, and veterans experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County

orgs.name: CHRYSALIS SHELTER FOR VICTIMS OF DOMESTIC VIOLENCE INC
services: Emergency shelter for people impacted by domestic violence and their children (confidential Phoenix location)
24/7 support line (602-955-9059, printed on own site as both office and 24/7 support number)
Transitional housing for up to two years
Advocacy, safety planning and case management; basic-needs assistance
Counseling for children and adults; on-site childcare at the emergency shelter
Mobile advocacy with legal services and court accompaniment; offender treatment and abuse-prevention programs
orgs.serves: Individuals and families impacted by domestic abuse in the Phoenix area (serving since 1981; 1,400+ survivors and family members a year per own site)

orgs.name: CIRCLE THE CITY
services: Medical respite care: two 50-bed centers where people experiencing homelessness recover from acute illness or injury with daily medical care, 24/7 nursing support, a bed, food and case management (an 85-bed East Valley center in Mesa is planned to open in 2026)
Outpatient primary and preventive healthcare at two clinics for people facing homelessness (walk-in and scheduled appointments)
Mobile medical units and street medicine teams delivering care at shelters, transitional living centers and unsheltered locations across Maricopa County
Hospital Health Navigator Program connecting patients to support services during and after hospital discharge
Integrated behavioral health services
orgs.serves: People experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County (about 8,000-9,000 people a year)

orgs.name: CITY OF PHOENIX EVICTION LEGAL SERVICES PROGRAM
services: City of Phoenix Human Services program giving eligible tenants free legal help with a current or former eviction crisis: limited or full legal representation in eviction court, mediation services, and post-eviction help clearing barriers to renting again

Eligibility as published: facing eviction or received a notice to vacate; income at or below 80% of Area Median Income (2025 HUD figures published on the page); living in Phoenix or receiving City of Phoenix water service
Apply online via the city's screening form, email HSD.EvictionHelp@phoenix.gov, call 602-262-7210, or get in-person help at the Travis L. Williams Family Services Center, 4732 S Central Ave, Phoenix
The city warns the Arizona eviction process is swift — answer calls and emails from the program quickly
orgs.serves: Phoenix residents facing eviction or dealing with a former eviction

orgs.name: COMMUNITY LEGAL SERVICES
services: Free legal assistance and representation for eligible Maricopa County tenants facing eviction for nonpayment of rent, funded by Maricopa County Human Services (Eviction Prevention Legal Assistance Program — the county set aside $2.6 million in ARPA funds for this partnership)
Legal information about tenant rights, landlord responsibilities, and the eviction process, including federal and subsidized-housing rules
Legal advice specific to the tenant's case, and representation in landlord negotiations, mediation, and eviction court (County Justice Courts and Superior Court)

CLS is a full civil legal-aid firm: its published practice areas also include housing law, family law, benefits, employment, consumer, and disability matters for low-income residents (per 211 Arizona's CLS program listings)
County renter line for this program: contact CLS directly at 602-385-8880
orgs.serves: Maricopa County residents at risk of eviction for nonpayment of rent; CLS's general civil legal aid serves low-income residents (generally at or below 125% of federal poverty guidelines)

orgs.name: DIOCESAN COUNCIL FOR THE SOCIETY OF ST VINCENT DE PAUL DIOCESE PHOENIX
services: Rent and utility bill assistance: help with rent, mortgage payments, or heat/water/gas utilities — the society reports $8.2 million in rent and utility assistance a year to help people avoid eviction (per its site, via Catholic Sun reporting of SVdP figures); start with the HOPE line 602-266-4673 or the Rent/Utility Assistance line 602-850-6948; neighborhood help runs through parish conferences across the Valley

Hot meals and food boxes: four charity dining rooms (including the Phoenix Dining Room / Human Services Campus dining room at 1075 W Jackson St and the main campus at 420 W Watkins Rd, Phoenix) serving thousands daily — the society reports about 2.5 million meals a year — plus food boxes delivered to families

Shelter and weather relief at locations across the Valley, including interim housing facilities and an emergency shelter; Resource Center at 320 W Watkins Rd offers clothing, hygiene, and showers (last sign-in 2:30 PM per the society's published resource sheet)

Also on its published resource sheet: ID and birth-certificate vouchers, Traveler's Aid, a Center for Family Wellness, medical and dental clinics for uninsured patients, and a medical-equipment loan closet — medical/dental care has no canonical tag and is described here, not tagged
AA/NA group meetings are hosted at the Phoenix Dining Room (per the society's own resource sheet) — meeting schedules belong to the fellowships; see the Salt River Intergroup and NA records
orgs.serves: people and families in need across central and northern Arizona, including people experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County

orgs.name: FAMILY HOUSING HUB
services: The family front door to Maricopa County's homeless-services system: one call connects families with children under 18 to assessment, diversion problem-solving, and referral to emergency shelter and housing programs across the county
Start by phone: call 2-1-1 (877-211-8661, 7 days a week) — the Hub's own site says you do not need to drive to an office unless 2-1-1 tells you to; Hub line 602-595-8700

Walk-in Coordinated Access Points include the Family Housing Hub at MesaCAN, 635 E. Broadway Rd, Mesa (Tue 9 AM-3 PM), the VA CRRC in Phoenix, City of Chandler Neighborhood Resources, and Tempe mobile outreach (Care Hope Line 480-350-8004)
Participating shelters named on the Hub site: CASS Vista Colina, Salvation Army Phoenix Emergency Shelter, UMOM New Day Centers, St. Vincent de Paul
Even when no shelter spot is open, the Hub connects families to food, work, and utility help and explains the next step; in extreme heat it points families to cooling sites
orgs.serves: families with children under 18 experiencing or at risk of homelessness anywhere in Maricopa County

orgs.name: HUMAN SERVICES CAMPUS INC
services: Operates the Key Campus (formerly Human Services Campus) in downtown Phoenix — a 24/7, low-barrier campus where close to 14,000 single adults a year get immediate needs resolved, a housing plan, and navigation through the process of ending their homelessness; the campus hosts the Brian Garcia Welcome Center, the Coordinated Entry access point for single adults

Keys to Change (the org's public name) runs prevention, intervention, and access-to-housing programs at Key Campus and throughout Maricopa County, in collaboration with the campus partner agencies (CASS shelter, St. Vincent de Paul dining room, health care, and others on site)
The org received a $10 million Maricopa County ARPA allocation to address homelessness (see fiscal map)
orgs.serves: single adults experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County

orgs.name: MARICOPA COUNTY COMMUNITY ACTION PROGRAM (CAP) — RENT & UTILITY ASSISTANCE
services: Maricopa County Human Services (Senior Services and Community Resilience Division) coordinates rental assistance — help with a rental deposit or monthly rental payment — for county residents living OUTSIDE Glendale, Mesa, and Phoenix, delivered through Community Action Program (CAP) offices throughout the county
The county's Human Services links page routes residents to companion Utility Assistance (Maricopa.gov/UtilityHelp), Homeless Services, and Legal Assistance for Renters from the same CAP/county system
Glendale, Mesa, and Phoenix residents are routed to their own city programs from the county page (Mesa's rental help runs through A New Leaf's MesaCAN; see fiscal map)

Apply through your local CAP office following the step-by-step instructions on the county page; the county also launched an online Client Portal for rental, mortgage, and utility assistance applications (hsdclientportal.maricopa.gov, per county Human Services newsletter)
orgs.serves: Maricopa County households outside Glendale, Mesa, and Phoenix needing help with rent, a rental deposit, or utilities

orgs.name: MARICOPA COUNTY EVICTION PREVENTION (MCEP) PILOT
services: County eviction-prevention pilot paying rental and utility arrears for renter households at the beginning of the eviction process, before a case hardens in court
Rental arrears: up to 2 months, not to exceed $3,000 (excluding late fees). Utility arrears: up to 2 months, not to exceed $1,000

Eligibility as published on the application: U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident; living in ZIP 85008, 85040, 85041, or 85042; temporary emergency or financial setback affecting ability to pay; able to pay rent/utilities going forward. Assistance subject to eligibility and available funding

Companion county layer: the FY2027 Eviction Prevention / Diversion Pilot ($800,000 county allocation, Board-approved May 2026, with the City of Phoenix providing utility assistance and case management) intervenes with justice courts and participating landlords in the same high-filing ZIP codes; HOM Inc. administers the program and engages property owners and residents
orgs.serves: renter households in Phoenix ZIPs 85008, 85040, 85041, and 85042 at risk of eviction for nonpayment

orgs.name: MARICOPA REGIONAL COORDINATED ENTRY
services: THE FRONT DOOR for homelessness help in Maricopa County (Maricopa Regional Continuum of Care). Coordinated Entry does not hand out rent checks itself — it is how the region's shelter and housing money is allocated, so start here
Single adults 18+: Brian Garcia Welcome Center, 206 S. 12th Ave, Phoenix (Mon-Fri 7:30 AM-11:00 PM) — walk-in Coordinated Entry access point on the Key Campus
Families with children under 18: Family Housing Hub, 602-595-8700 (see separate record) — do not use the single-adult points
Native American individuals: Native American Connections access point, 602-648-9739; youth 18-26: NAC HomeBase, 602-263-5531

Other access points listed on the official page: Community Bridges 877-931-9142, CASS Glendale 623-207-8902, CBI PATH outreach (mental-illness street outreach) 844-691-5948, Phoenix Rescue Mission outreach 602-346-3361, A New Leaf East Valley Men's Center 480-610-6722, UMOM Halle Women's Center 602-362-5833, VA Community Resource Referral Center (veterans) 602-248-6040, St. Vincent de Paul Watkins Rd, City of Chandler 480-782-4349, City of Tempe HOPE outreach 480-858-7993
orgs.serves: people experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County — single adults, families, youth, veterans, and Native American individuals (each through its own access point)

orgs.name: NATIVE AMERICAN CONNECTIONS INC
services: Coordinated Entry access point for Native American individuals experiencing homelessness: start a housing assessment in the Coordinated Entry System with NAC's Housing Specialist at 602-648-9739 (PSHinquiry@nativeconnections.org)
Coordinated Entry access point for youth ages 18-26, with services at NAC's HomeBase locations: call 602-263-5531 to get started
NAC's page is also the published official list of Maricopa County Coordinated Entry access points (used for the Coordinated Entry system record)
orgs.serves: Native American individuals experiencing homelessness, and youth ages 18-26 experiencing homelessness, in Maricopa County

orgs.name: PHOENIX RESCUE MISSION
services: Christ-centered help for people struggling with homelessness, addiction, trauma, or hunger — entry point is the Mission's Get Help page; main line 602-233-3000; street outreach (Hope Coaches) hotline 602-346-3361
Short-term care: Rescue-Assess-Place (RAP) — a brief residential crisis-intervention stay with a confidential case-manager meeting to match the person to programs
Transformations: a year-long residential recovery program for freedom from addiction, built around the individual's needs
Hope Coach mobile outreach: vehicles travel Maricopa County streets with lifesaving water, basic needs, and on-demand case management; the Mission is also a Coordinated Entry outreach access point

Hope for Hunger Food Bank (near downtown Glendale): emergency food, case management, and job assistance for more than 250 households a day, plus mobile food pantries serving Valley food deserts weekly
Specialized services on its site: work programs, criminal-justice diversion, and housing placement
orgs.serves: people experiencing homelessness, addiction, trauma, or hunger in Maricopa County

orgs.name: SALT RIVER INTERGROUP INC
services: Salt River Intergroup of Alcoholics Anonymous — the AA central office serving Phoenix and Scottsdale: maintains the official AA meeting list for the Phoenix/Scottsdale area (about 1,600 meetings a week in the Valley per its newsletter) — schedules are maintained by the Intergroup, linked here, not scraped
24/7 AA Help Line: (602) 264-1341 — call any time to talk to an AA member or find a meeting; central office (602) 264-1374, 3215 E Thunderbird Rd Ste B, Phoenix
AA literature and bookstore at the central office; Intergroup service committees (Hospitals & Institutions, Public Information / Cooperation with the Professional Community, Grapevine, archives)
orgs.serves: people with a desire to stop drinking, and their families, in Phoenix, Scottsdale, and the surrounding Valley

orgs.name: SAVE THE FAMILY FOUNDATION OF ARIZONA
services: Transitional and rapid re-housing for families experiencing homelessness (Rapid Re-housing, Tenant Based Rental Assistance, and Step Up to Independence programs; 24-month Step Up track with case management)
Stepped rental subsidies and housing-location help to secure leased rental housing (Mesa ESG rapid-rehousing award, FY2025-26 and FY26/27 city funding recommendations)
Career services and employment support for parents
Budgeting and financial-literacy classes, parenting classes and life-skills classes
In-house mental health support and substance-use support referrals
Children's services: food, school supplies, individual education plans, counseling and drop-in child care
Affordable Rental Movement (ARM) income-based affordable housing with supportive services (separate affiliated entity, EIN 860710822)
orgs.serves: Families with children experiencing homelessness or housing insecurity in Mesa and the East Valley (Mesa, Gilbert, Chandler, Tempe, Scottsdale); veteran families (Valor on Eighth)

orgs.name: ST JOSEPH THE WORKER
services: Employment services: one-on-one job-search support, resumes, job leads, computers and interview preparation (offices at 382 E Palm Lane #150, Phoenix, and 1833 W Main St #128, Mesa)
Transportation support and bus passes for job seekers
Uniforms, work clothing, tools and financial assistance for professional certification/licensure fees
Workforce Villages: 12-week employment-first transitional housing program (clients save 80% of paychecks toward their own housing)
Mobile Success Unit: a job-development office on wheels visiting 16 Valley locations monthly, including reentry stops
Credit consultation and financial-literacy coaching
orgs.serves: People experiencing homelessness or extreme economic hardship who want to work, across the Phoenix metro (founded 1988; about 2,900 connections to full-time jobs in FY2024-25 per own site)

orgs.name: ST MARYS FOOD BANK ALLIANCE
services: Food distribution through 600+ partner nonprofits statewide, with a Find Food search by ZIP code
Emergency food boxes, including home delivery of emergency food boxes in Maricopa, Yavapai and Pinal counties
Children's feeding programs (school-year and summer feeding sites)
Mobile pantry distributions
Skills Center job training in warehouse logistics and food service for adults in need
orgs.serves: People facing food insecurity across Arizona, including Maricopa County; HQ and main distribution center in Phoenix (2831 N 31st Ave)

orgs.name: UNITED FOOD BANK
services: Food distribution through 125+ partner food pantries, mobile food truck markets and hot meal sites across Arizona, concentrated in the East Valley
Emergency food bags and community food distributions (Neighbor's Pantry distributions in Mesa)
